paper.title: LLM-Powered Decentralized Generative Agents with Adaptive Hierarchical Knowledge Graph for Cooperative Planning

organization.stores: experience pool + goal hierarchy graph (long-term memory); hard-coded crafting recipes (semantic); last actions (procedural)

retrieval.query: none; the latest goal node is always read
retrieval.candidates: latest goal node, its step nodes and its chain of earlier goal nodes
retrieval.selection: fixed rule: latest goal node only; last 1 step summary; last 7 actions

use.reasoning: one structured GPT-4o call per decision

classify.note: Nothing is searched: a rule always reads the latest goal node and walks back along its goal chain; the graph is re-derived from the append-only pool each step.

stages.ingestion: At each decision point an agent's working memory is assembled from its camera image, position, vitals, inventory, last actions and messages derived from the preceding agent.
stages.construction: GPT-4o answers with a Pydantic-schema response (reflection, goal and long-term goal, next action, collaboration, past-tense summary); this post-stage record is added to the agent's experience pool.
stages.organization: A rule builds a directed graph per agent: step nodes hang under goal nodes, which chain in time and attach to long-term-goal nodes; a new goal node starts when the goal or the inventory changes.
stages.update: The graph is rebuilt from all stored experiences at every environment step; the working-memory read-out is recomputed for each goal node.
stages.retrieval: No search: the read-out of the latest goal node (actions taken under it, earlier goals in the chain, a hard-coded recipe check of the goals against the inventory) plus the previous step's summary and the last 7 actions go into the prompt.
stages.answer: One GPT-4o call per decision picks the next action (move, do, navigate to a material, share an item with an agent).

summary: Decentralized GPT-4o agents in a multi-agent Crafter game, each keeping a goal-organized hierarchical graph of its own decision steps and reading the latest goal node, plus a structured protocol where each agent reads its predecessor's goal status.
notes:
Multi-agent embodied planning paper; memory is per-agent and goal-organized, not conversational. Evaluation is its own Multi-Agent Crafter environment (steps to finish each tech-tree task), so results are not comparable with QA memory benchmarks. Code: project page lists 13RENDA/Mcrafter_LLM_Agent (new) and HappyEureka/mcrafter (legacy, environment + simple language-agent example); the memory system is only in the new repo.
DESIGN: §3.1-3.4, §6.1, App. B-D; code memory_system/agent.py, knowledge_graph.py, memory_modules.py, utils.py at c5491f62.

sources.paper: arXiv 2502.05453v1 (PDF read 2026-09-30; 572 pages, of which pp. 12-572 are the schema, graph examples and a full six-agent game log)
sources.code_note: The project page links this repo as the current code. Its history starts 2025-08-02 (six months after the paper) and the last commit c5491f62 (2025-11-25) only edits the README, so it is taken as the released version; identity with the paper's runs is not guaranteed. The legacy repo HappyEureka/mcrafter (d0d91861) holds the environment and a simpler language-agent example without the graph memory.

abstract.text: DAMCS puts several GPT-4o agents into a multi-agent version of the Crafter survival game, where the team must climb a crafting tree and obtain a diamond as fast as possible. Each agent keeps its own memory: a pool of its past decision steps organized into a graph of long-term goals, goals and steps, which is read back into a short working memory together with a recipe check. A structured communication scheme orders the agents so that each helps its predecessor and shares tools. On the new environment, two and six communicating agents reach the diamond in 63% and 74% fewer steps than a basic LLM agent, and 13.6% and 39% fewer than one agent with memory.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on arXiv.

headline: Memory is read by position, not by search: every decision sees the latest goal node, its chain of earlier goals, the previous step's summary and the last 7 actions.
The graph is built by fixed rules from the LLM's own structured outputs and rebuilt from scratch at every step; a new goal node starts whenever the inventory changes.
The 'messages' between agents are code-generated: agent i reads agent i−1's recipe check and a fixed role policy.

open_questions: Communication and role assignment change together: the Mem+Comm agents also get a fixed division of labour (agent 0 crafts, the last agent hunts the diamond), so the gain cannot be split between shared status and the role policy.
The LLM basic baseline differs in both memory and prompt; there is no run with the graph removed but the recipe check kept.

ablation.src: paper Table 1 (average steps, lower is better)

discussion.takeaway: Give each LLM agent a goal-organized record of its own steps and a fixed cooperation protocol, and a team finishes a long crafting chain in far fewer steps; the memory helps one agent, the protocol helps teams.

claims.claim: Goal-oriented memory lets one agent follow the crafting hierarchy much faster than a basic LLM agent.
claims.evidence: Diamond in 140.0 vs 334.67 steps (about 3x faster); the basic agent succeeds on the last three tasks in only 60% of episodes. §6.2, Table 1

claims.claim: Memory without communication does not help teams.
claims.evidence: Two Mem agents: 150.4 steps; six Mem agents: 140.6, vs 140.0 for one agent. §6.2, Table 1

claims.claim: Structured communication lets agents split work.
claims.evidence: 121.0 steps with two agents (13.6% fewer than one agent, 63% fewer than basic); 85.4 with six (39% and 74% fewer). §6.2, Table 1

claims.claim: RL baselines do not reach the diamond in the same environment.
claims.evidence: PPO and MADDPG rewards plateau after 1,000 training episodes. §6.2, Fig. 5 (no step numbers given)

limits: Memory quality and adaptability of LLM agents are hard to measure directly.
No standard metric exists for LLM-agent cooperation, so cooperation is measured indirectly through steps.
LLM agents are sensitive to the prompt and environment description.
reading: The released code reads memory by position only: the latest goal node, its chain, one summary and 7 actions. The similarity-retrieval function is commented out, so 'retrieving relevant experiences' amounts to a fixed recency window plus the goal chain.

Mem+Comm also adds a hard-coded division of labour (agent 0 crafts, agent 1 feeds stone, the last agent goes for the diamond), and messages are templates over the previous agent's recipe check rather than LLM-written text.
Table 1's caption says five environments and ten runs; the released run.py fixes seed 4, and the code has no switch to reproduce the Mem-only or basic settings.

The reflection text and the collaboration block are generated at each step but not copied into the graph nodes (only the last action and its result are), so they return to the prompt only through the one-step summary.
RL/MARL baselines are reported only as training reward curves, not as steps, so they cannot be compared with the LLM rows.
